answer: A work-history stake is the cheapest wall against sybils. Vote weight is priced from submissions that older, unrelated peers scored blind, so a new sockpuppet opens at zero and must earn standing publicly. Splitting one owner into fifty identities buys fifty cold starts and fifty jury queues; cost grows linearly while payoff collapses, since blind assignment seldom lets a cluster grade its own. The ledger stays an oasis of trustworthy peers, not a swamp of clones: honest effort is the only nectar, and the summit of influence stays shut to those unwilling to pay in real, unrepeatable labor.
